statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 24% sits at the top of the watch band, still below the 25% block threshold, while Stress 57% remains elevated.
recommendation: The rate and oil impulse re-extended to session highs in the last hour, yet the Nasdaq-100 has not made a new low with it and still trades above the level set two hours ago. That non-confirmation is why Tail is held at the top of the watch band rather than moved into the block range. The narrow published danger window covers the 17:00Z seven-year note auction and its immediate digestion.
headline: Long-end yields and oil re-extend to session highs while the Nasdaq-100 holds above its opening low
body:
NDX cash trades near 30,245, about -0.74% on the day, inside a 30,204 to 30,346 session range roughly two hours into the US cash day. The index gave back the bounce it held an hour ago and now sits in the lower half of that range, but it is still 42 points above the 30,204 low set shortly after the open and has not produced a new session low. NQ December futures near 30,521 (-0.79%) hold about 151 points above the 30,370 overnight low inside a 30,370-30,813 range, so neither contract is at a session extreme. VIX near 16.08 is up about 5.9% and rising, yet remains below its 16.57 session high.

The amplifier side has genuinely worsened since the previous hour. The 10-year yield at 5.15% and the 30-year at 5.44% both print at the top of today's 5.09-5.15 and 5.39-5.44 ranges, taking out the earlier intraday peak and marking the highest levels since 2007 and 2004 respectively. WTI crude near $95.89 is up about 4.05% and close to its $95.98 session high, with Brent above $100, after Iran's president said Tehran would restrict freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while US sanctions and a blockade remain in place. Initial jobless claims for the week ending September 19 came in at 197,000 against a 201,000 consensus and 198,000 prior, and August new home sales ran at a 684,000 annual rate, both feeding the resilient-demand read behind this week's rate repricing. New York Fed President Williams called a further increase by year end reasonable and Philadelphia's Paulson said some modest further tightening may be warranted, with October odds near 69%. Shared Finviz context collected at 12:21Z is more than three hours old and therefore stale under the provider contract, and its futures section was unavailable, so it is not used as current evidence here.

The defining question for this contract is whether the price path denies retracement, and it currently does not. Yields and oil are at session extremes while the index is not, which is a divergence rather than the aligned one-way structure that Tail measures. No sequence of shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements has been observed in NQ; the contract has spent two hours in a 443-point range. Tail therefore rises from 21% to 24% to reflect the re-extended amplifier stack and the unresolved 17:00Z auction, and stops below the block threshold because the equity price path has not confirmed. Stress rises to 57% on the oil move, the multi-decade yield highs and the rising VIX.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours opened with a yellow plateau near 21-24% Tail through Wednesday's US afternoon and evening, eased to three green hours between 01:00Z and 03:00Z as Asian trade stayed orderly, and rebuilt from the European open. Risk peaked at 25% Tail and 58% Stress at 09:00Z as the 30-year yield pushed to a post-2004 high, then held a 22-24% band through the US pre-market before easing to 21% at 14:00Z on the opening-hour retracement. Stress stayed in a 47-58% range throughout, the signature of a difficult but still mean-reverting environment rather than a persistent one-way path.
outlookSummary: Tail is published in the watch band for most of the horizon and steps to 25% for the single 17:00Z hour covering the seven-year note auction, which is the narrow published danger window. It eases through auction digestion and the US close, then falls into the 17-19% green band overnight once the scheduled calendar is exhausted. Risk rebuilds from the European open on Friday toward 22% into the 12:30Z durable goods release, the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z final Michigan sentiment reading. Confidence decays from 87% to 79% with distance from the assessment time. Every forecast hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.

The rate and oil impulse has re-extended, but the index has not made a new low with it.
